name: Baanah and Rechab
charge: Murder of Ish-bosheth on his bed at noon, and carrying his head to David for a reward
summary: When Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled. Two captains of his own bands came about the heat of the day as though they would fetch wheat, smote him under the fifth rib as he lay on his bed at noon, beheaded him, and carried the head all night through the plain to David at Hebron, calling it the head of the king’s enemy. They did too much. David required the blood of a righteous person slain in his own house upon his bed, and they were slain, dismembered and hanged up over the pool.
offenseFull: When Saul’s son Ish-bosheth heard that Abner was dead in Hebron his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled. He had two men that were captains of bands, Baanah and Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin (2 Samuel 4:1-2). The sons of Rimmon came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, who lay on a bed at noon in the hottest part of the day; they came into the midst of the house as though they would have fetched wheat, and smote him under the fifth rib, and escaped. They beheaded him, took his head, and got away through the plain all night (2 Samuel 4:5-12). His own captains, who had a right to be in the house, used that access to kill him while he rested. They brought the head to David at Hebron and presented it as the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul his enemy, who sought his life, and said that the Lord had avenged the king that day of Saul and of his seed (2 Samuel 4:8). They did too much; they went overboard. Israel being out of order took the matter into their own hands. David had no quarrel with Saul’s sons; it was Saul who sought his life. They called murder the vengeance of the Lord, and expected the new king to pay them for it.
judgmentFull: David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, swearing by the Lord who had redeemed his soul out of all adversity: when one told him Saul was dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, he took hold of him and slew him in Ziklag, and that was the reward he gave him for his tidings; how much more, when wicked men had slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed, should he not require his blood of their hand and take them away from the earth? (2 Samuel 4:9-12). The man was at rest, asleep, and it was not even a contest between men for the kingdom; that is not how the Most High brings His purpose to pass. So David commanded his young men, and they slew them, cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron; but they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner. The murderers were publicly judged, and the head they had carried as a token for reward was given a burial.

The law knows what they did by its name. If a man comes presumptuously upon his neighbour to slay him with guile, he is to be taken even from the altar of the Lord that he may die (Exodus 21:14), and a curse stands on the man that smites his neighbour secretly (Deuteronomy 27:24). This is a large part of why David is called a man after the Most High’s own heart: he did not accept wickedness done in his name, and he did not let murderers slide because the killing happened to suit him. He called them out, and they received judgment for taking a man’s life not ordained of the Lord nor commanded by the king. Let all things be done decently and in order (1 Corinthians 14:40). The same distinction governed his last charge to Solomon concerning Joab, who shed the blood of war in peace (1 Kings 2:5-6). Two captains who had read the king’s advantage as their own licence misjudged both the king and the Lord whose name they used.

lawsResolved.text: If a man acts with premeditation against his neighbor, to kill him with guile, he shall die.
Killing for hire is condemned (the assassin and the one who hires him are both guilty of murder).
Government officers that engage in conspiracy, treachery and murder are to be put to death.

text.text: And when Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

And Saul’s son had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin:
And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish–bosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.
And they came thither into the midst of the house, as though they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him under the fifth rib: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and gat them away through the plain all night.

And they brought the head of Ish–bosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ish–bosheth the son of Saul thine enemy, which sought thy life; and the Lord hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.
And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As the Lord liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who thought that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:
How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?

And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish–bosheth, and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.

And they brought the head of Ish–bosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ish–bosheth the son of Saul thine enemy, which sought thy life; and the Lord hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.
And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As the Lord liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who thought that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:
How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?

And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish–bosheth, and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.
But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.
Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen.
Let all things be done decently and in order.

Moreover thou knowest also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, and what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Israel, unto Abner the son of Ner, and unto Amasa the son of Jether, whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war upon his girdle that was about his loins, and in his shoes that were on his feet.
Do therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace.
